metadata.title: Exact Matrix Completion via Convex Optimization

nodes.name: Matrix Completion Problem
nodes.statement: Recover a data matrix $\mtx{M} \in \mathbb{R}^{n_1 \times n_2}$ from $m \ll n_1 n_2$ of its entries observed at locations $(i,j) \in \Omega$.
nodes.statement_clean: Reconstruct an unknown matrix from a subset of its entries.

nodes.name: Rank Minimization Program
nodes.statement: $\min_{\mtx{X}} \rank(\mtx{X})$ subject to $X_{ij} = M_{ij}$ for $(i,j) \in \Omega$.
nodes.statement_clean: Find the minimum-rank matrix consistent with observed entries.

nodes.name: Nuclear Norm Minimization
nodes.statement: $\min_{\mtx{X}} \|\mtx{X}\|_*$ subject to $X_{ij} = M_{ij}$ for $(i,j) \in \Omega$, where $\|\mtx{X}\|_* = \sum_k \sigma_k(\mtx{X})$.
nodes.statement_clean: Convex relaxation of rank minimization using the nuclear norm.

nodes.name: Generalized Low-Rank Recovery from Linear Measurements
nodes.statement: $\min_{\mtx{X}} \rank(\mtx{X})$ subject to $\vct{f}_i^* \mtx{X} \vct{g}_j = \vct{f}_i^* \mtx{M} \vct{g}_j$ for $(i,j) \in \Omega$, with bases $\{\vct{f}_i\}, \{\vct{g}_j\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Extension of matrix completion to recovery from arbitrary inner-product measurements.

nodes.name: Nuclear Norm
nodes.statement: $\|\mtx{X}\|_* = \sum_{k=1}^n \sigma_k(\mtx{X})$, the sum of singular values.

nodes.name: Coherence of a Subspace
nodes.statement: For a subspace $U \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ of dimension $r$ with orthogonal projection $\mtx{P}_U$, the coherence is $\mu(U) \equiv \frac{n}{r} \max_{1 \le i \le n} \|\mtx{P}_U \vct{e}_i\|^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Coherence measures how aligned a subspace is with the standard basis; ranges in $[1, n/r]$.

nodes.name: Random Orthogonal Model
nodes.statement: Low-rank matrix model where the singular vectors $\{\vct{u}_k\}, \{\vct{v}_k\}$ are selected uniformly at random among all families of $r$ orthonormal vectors; singular values arbitrary.

nodes.name: Incoherent Basis Model
nodes.statement: $\mtx{M} = \sum_{k=1}^r \epsilon_k \sigma_k \vct{u}_k \vct{v}_k^*$ with $\{\epsilon_k\}$ a random sign sequence and $\{\vct{u}_k\}, \{\vct{v}_k\}$ having entries of magnitude at most $\sqrt{\mu_B/n}$.

nodes.name: Tangent Space $T$ and Projector $\PT$
nodes.statement: $T$ is the linear span of matrices of the form $\vct{u}_k \vct{x}^*$ and $\vct{y} \vct{v}_k^*$, with $\dim T = r(n_1+n_2-r)$. The projector is $\PT(\mtx{X}) = \mtx{P}_U \mtx{X} + \mtx{X} \mtx{P}_V - \mtx{P}_U \mtx{X} \mtx{P}_V$.

nodes.name: Sampling Operator $\PO$
nodes.statement: Orthogonal projector onto observed indices: $[\PO(\mtx{X})]_{ij} = X_{ij}$ if $(i,j) \in \Omega$ and $0$ otherwise. Also written $\mathcal{R}_\Omega(\mtx{X}) = (X_{ij})_{(i,j) \in \Omega}$.

nodes.name: Subgradient of Nuclear Norm
nodes.statement: $\mtx{Y} \in \partial \|\mtx{X}_0\|_*$ iff $\PT(\mtx{Y}) = \sum_k \vct{u}_k \vct{v}_k^*$ and $\|\PTc(\mtx{Y})\| \le 1$.

nodes.name: Bernoulli Sampling Model
nodes.statement: $\Omega' = \{(i,j) : \delta_{ij} = 1\}$ where $\delta_{ij}$ are i.i.d. Bernoulli with $\P(\delta_{ij}=1) = p = m/(n_1 n_2)$.

nodes.name: Schatten q-Norm
nodes.statement: $\|\mtx{X}\|_{S_q} = (\sum_{i=1}^n \sigma_i(\mtx{X})^q)^{1/q}$. Schatten-1 = nuclear norm, Schatten-2 = Frobenius, Schatten-$\infty$ = spectral norm.

nodes.name: Coherence Assumptions A0 and A1
nodes.statement: (A0) $\max(\mu(U), \mu(V)) \le \mu_0$. (A1) $\|\sum_{k=1}^r \vct{u}_k \vct{v}_k^*\|_\infty \le \mu_1 \sqrt{r/(n_1 n_2)}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Standing incoherence conditions on the column/row spaces and on their associated 'sign matrix'.

nodes.name: Main Recovery Theorem (Random Orthogonal Model)
nodes.statement: For $\mtx{M} \in \mathbb{R}^{n_1 \times n_2}$ of rank $r$ from the random orthogonal model with $n = \max(n_1,n_2)$, if $m \ge C n^{5/4} r \log n$ then \eqref{eq:sdp} recovers $\mtx{M}$ uniquely w.p. $\ge 1 - c n^{-3}$; if also $r \le n^{1/5}$, the bound improves to $m \ge C n^{6/5} r \log n$.
assumptions: $\mtx{M}$ is $n_1 \times n_2$ of rank $r$ from random orthogonal model
$\Omega$ sampled uniformly at random of size $m$
conclusions: If $m \ge C n^{5/4} r \log n$, the minimizer of $\min \|\mtx{X}\|_*$ s.t. $\PO(\mtx{X}) = \PO(\mtx{M})$ is unique and equals $\mtx{M}$ w.p. $\ge 1 - c n^{-3}$
If additionally $r \le n^{1/5}$, then $m \ge C n^{6/5} r \log n$ suffices

nodes.name: General Recovery Theorem (Incoherent Matrices)
nodes.statement: For $\mtx{M}$ of rank $r$ obeying A0 and A1, $n = \max(n_1,n_2)$: if $m \ge C \max(\mu_1^2, \mu_0^{1/2} \mu_1, \mu_0 n^{1/4}) \, n r (\beta \log n)$ for $\beta>2$, then nuclear-norm minimization recovers $\mtx{M}$ uniquely w.p. $\ge 1 - c n^{-\beta}$; for $r \le \mu_0^{-1} n^{1/5}$, $m \ge C \mu_0 n^{6/5} r (\beta \log n)$ suffices.
conclusions: Nuclear norm minimizer is unique and equals $\mtx{M}$ with probability at least $1 - c n^{-\beta}$ when $m \ge C \max(\mu_1^2, \mu_0^{1/2} \mu_1, \mu_0 n^{1/4}) n r (\beta \log n)$
For $r \le \mu_0^{-1} n^{1/5}$, the bound improves to $m \ge C \mu_0 n^{6/5} r (\beta \log n)$

nodes.name: Rudelson-Type Near-Isometry
nodes.statement: Under the Bernoulli model with $\max(\mu(U),\mu(V)) \le \mu_0$, $p^{-1} \|\PT \PO \PT - p \PT\| \le C_R \sqrt{\mu_0 nr (\beta \log n)/m}$ w.p. $\ge 1 - 3 n^{-\beta}$, provided the right-hand side is $<1$.
assumptions: Bernoulli sampling model with parameter $p = m/(n_1 n_2)$
conclusions: $p^{-1} \|\PT \PO \PT - p \PT\| \le C_R \sqrt{\mu_0 nr (\beta \log n)/m}$ with probability at least $1 - 3 n^{-\beta}$

nodes.name: Bernoulli Deviation Bound (Theorem on $\PO$)
nodes.statement: For any fixed $n \times n$ matrix $\mtx{X}$ and $\beta > 2$, $p^{-1}\|(\PO - p\OpId)(\mtx{X})\| \le C_0 \sqrt{\beta n \log n / p} \, \|\mtx{X}\|_\infty$ w.p. $\ge 1 - n^{-\beta}$, provided $np \ge \beta \log n$.
conclusions: $p^{-1}\|(\PO - p\OpId)(\mtx{X})\| \le C_0 \sqrt{\beta n \log n / p} \, \|\mtx{X}\|_\infty$ with probability at least $1 - n^{-\beta}$

nodes.name: Rudelson Selection Theorem
nodes.statement: For $\{\delta_{ab}\}$ i.i.d. Bernoulli($p$), if $\|\PT(\eab)\|_F^2 \le 2\mu_0 r/n$, then $\E Z \le C'_R \sqrt{\mu_0 nr \log n / m}$ when the bound is $<1$, plus a Talagrand-type concentration bound for $|Z - \E Z|$.
assumptions: Right-hand side $C'_R \sqrt{\mu_0 nr \log n / m}$ is $< 1$
conclusions: $\E Z \le C'_R \sqrt{\mu_0 nr \log n / m}$
$\P(|Z - \E Z| > \lambda \sqrt{\mu_0 nr \log n / m}) \le 3 \exp(-\gamma'_0 \min\{\lambda^2 \log n, \lambda \sqrt{m \log n / (\mu_0 nr)}\})$

nodes.name: Incoherent Bases Span Incoherent Subspaces
nodes.statement: Matrices from the incoherent basis model satisfy A1 with $\mu_1 \le C \mu_B \sqrt{(\beta+2) \log n}$ w.p. $\ge 1 - c n^{-\beta}$.
conclusions: Assumption A1 holds with $\mu_1 \le C \mu_B \sqrt{(\beta+2) \log n}$ with probability at least $1 - c n^{-\beta}$

nodes.name: Random Orthogonal Model Coherence Bounds
nodes.statement: Set $\bar r = \max(r, \log n)$. The random orthogonal model obeys $\max_i \|\mtx{P}_U \vct{e}_i\|^2 \le C \bar r/n$ and $\|\sum_k \vct{u}_k \vct{v}_k^*\|_\infty \le C \log n \sqrt{\bar r}/n$, w.p. $\ge 1 - c n^{-3} \log n$.
assumptions: $\mtx{M}$ sampled from the random orthogonal model
conclusions: $\max_i \|\mtx{P}_U \vct{e}_i\|^2 \le C \bar r / n$
$\|\sum_{1 \le k \le r} \vct{u}_k \vct{v}_k^*\|_\infty \le C \log n \sqrt{\bar r}/n$ with probability $\ge 1 - c n^{-3} \log n$

nodes.name: Chi-Squared Concentration
nodes.statement: For $Y_d \sim \chi^2_d$ and $t > 0$: $\P(Y_d - d \ge t \sqrt{2d} + t^2) \le e^{-t^2/2}$ and $\P(Y_d - d \le -t \sqrt{2d}) \le e^{-t^2/2}$.
conclusions: $\P(Y_d - d \ge t \sqrt{2d} + t^2) \le e^{-t^2/2}$
$\P(Y_d - d \le -t \sqrt{2d}) \le e^{-t^2/2}$

nodes.name: Uniqueness via Dual Certificate
nodes.statement: If $\mtx{X}_0 = \sum_k \sigma_k \vct{u}_k \vct{v}_k^*$ is feasible, and (1) there exists $\lambda$ with $\mtx{Y} = \mathcal{R}^*_\Omega \lambda$ obeying $\PT(\mtx{Y}) = \sum_k \vct{u}_k \vct{v}_k^*$ and $\|\PTc(\mtx{Y})\| < 1$, and (2) $\mathcal{R}_\Omega$ restricted to $T$ is injective, then $\mtx{X}_0$ is the unique minimizer of \eqref{eq:sdp}.
assumptions: $\mtx{X}_0 = \sum_{k=1}^r \sigma_k \vct{u}_k \vct{v}_k^*$ of rank $r$ is feasible for the nuclear-norm program
Sampling operator $\mathcal{R}_\Omega$ restricted to $T$ is injective
conclusions: $\mtx{X}_0$ is the unique minimizer of the nuclear-norm minimization problem

nodes.name: Nuclear-Spectral Duality
nodes.statement: For each pair $\mtx{W}, \mtx{H}$: $\<\mtx{W}, \mtx{H}\> \le \|\mtx{W}\| \|\mtx{H}\|_*$, and equality is achieved by some $\mtx{W}$ with $\|\mtx{W}\|=1$.
conclusions: There exists $\mtx{W}$ with $\|\mtx{W}\| = 1$ achieving equality

nodes.name: Bound on $\|\PO \PT\|$
nodes.statement: Under TP103.3 with $C_R \sqrt{\mu_0 nr (\log n)/m} \le 1/2$: $\|\PO \PT(\mtx{X})\|_F \le \sqrt{3p/2} \|\PT(\mtx{X})\|_F$.
conclusions: $\|\PO \PT(\mtx{X})\|_F \le \sqrt{3p/2} \|\PT(\mtx{X})\|_F$ for all $\mtx{X}$

nodes.name: Order-0 Spectral Bound
nodes.statement: If $m \ge \lambda \mu_1^2 nr \beta \log n$ for $\beta \ge 2$, $\lambda \ge 1$, then $p^{-1} \|(\PTc \PO \PT) \mtx{E}\| \le C_0 \lambda^{-1/2}$ w.p. $\ge 1 - n^{-\beta}$.
conclusions: $p^{-1} \|(\PTc \PO \PT) \mtx{E}\| \le C_0 \lambda^{-1/2}$ with probability at least $1 - n^{-\beta}$

nodes.name: Order-1 Spectral Bound
nodes.statement: If $m \ge \lambda \mu_1 \max(\sqrt{\mu_0}, \mu_1) nr \beta \log n$ for $\beta \ge 2, \lambda \ge 1$, then $p^{-1} \|(\PTc \PO \PT) \mathcal{H}(\mtx{E})\| \le C_1 \lambda^{-1}$ w.p. $\ge 1 - c_1 n^{-\beta}$.
conclusions: $p^{-1} \|(\PTc \PO \PT) \mathcal{H}(\mtx{E})\| \le C_1 \lambda^{-1}$ with probability at least $1 - c_1 n^{-\beta}$

nodes.name: Order-2 Spectral Bound
nodes.statement: If $m \ge \lambda \mu_0^{4/3} n r^{4/3} \beta \log n$, then $p^{-1} \|(\PTc \PO \PT) \mathcal{H}^2(\mtx{E})\| \le C_2 \lambda^{-3/2}$ w.p. $\ge 1 - c_2 n^{-\beta}$.
conclusions: $p^{-1} \|(\PTc \PO \PT) \mathcal{H}^2(\mtx{E})\| \le C_2 \lambda^{-3/2}$ with probability at least $1 - c_2 n^{-\beta}$

nodes.name: Order-3 Spectral Bound
nodes.statement: If $m \ge \lambda \mu_0^2 n r^2 \beta \log n$, then $p^{-1} \|(\PTc \PO \PT) \mathcal{H}^3(\mtx{E})\| \le C_3 \lambda^{-1/2}$ w.p. $\ge 1 - c_3 n^{-\beta}$.
conclusions: $p^{-1} \|(\PTc \PO \PT) \mathcal{H}^3(\mtx{E})\| \le C_3 \lambda^{-1/2}$ with probability at least $1 - c_3 n^{-\beta}$

nodes.name: Higher-Order Tail Bound
nodes.statement: If $m \ge (2C_R)^2 \mu_0 nr \beta \log n$, then $p^{-1} \|(\PTc \PO \PT) \sum_{k \ge k_0} \mathcal{H}^k(\mtx{E})\| \le C_{k_0} (n^2 r/m)^{1/2} (\mu_0 nr \beta \log n / m)^{k_0/2}$ w.p. $\ge 1 - n^{-\beta}$.
conclusions: $p^{-1} \|(\PTc \PO \PT) \sum_{k \ge k_0} \mathcal{H}^k(\mtx{E})\| \le C_{k_0} (n^2 r/m)^{1/2} (\mu_0 nr \beta \log n / m)^{k_0/2}$ with probability at least $1 - n^{-\beta}$

nodes.name: Noncommutative Khintchine Inequality
nodes.statement: For matrices $\mtx{X}_i$ and Rademacher signs $\epsilon_i$, $q \ge 2$: $[\E_\epsilon \|\sum_i \epsilon_i \mtx{X}_i\|_{S_q}^q]^{1/q} \le C_K \sqrt{q} \max(\|(\sum_i \mtx{X}_i^* \mtx{X}_i)^{1/2}\|_{S_q}, \|(\sum_i \mtx{X}_i \mtx{X}_i^*)^{1/2}\|_{S_q})$, $C_K = 2^{-1/4} \sqrt{\pi/e}$.
assumptions: $(\mtx{X}_i)$ a finite sequence of matrices of the same dimension
conclusions: $[\E_\epsilon \|\sum_i \epsilon_i \mtx{X}_i\|_{S_q}^q]^{1/q} \le C_K \sqrt{q} \max(\|(\sum_i \mtx{X}_i^* \mtx{X}_i)^{1/2}\|_{S_q}, \|(\sum_i \mtx{X}_i \mtx{X}_i^*)^{1/2}\|_{S_q})$ with $C_K = 2^{-1/4} \sqrt{\pi/e}$

nodes.name: Decoupling Inequality
nodes.statement: For independent $\{\eta_i\}$ and elements $x_{ij}$: $\P(\|\sum_{i \ne j} \eta_i \eta_j x_{ij}\| \ge t) \le C_D \P(\|\sum_{i \ne j} \eta_i \eta'_j x_{ij}\| > t/C_D)$, with $\{\eta'_i\}$ an independent copy.
assumptions: $\{x_{ij}\}_{i \ne j}$ elements of a Banach space
conclusions: $\P(\|\sum_{i \ne j} \eta_i \eta_j x_{ij}\| \ge t) \le C_D \P(\|\sum_{i \ne j} \eta_i \eta'_j x_{ij}\| > t/C_D)$

nodes.name: Bernstein-Type Bound on $\mathcal{Q}(\mtx{X})$
nodes.statement: $[\mathcal{Q}(\mtx{X})]_{ab} = p^{-1} \sum_{(a',b') \ne (a,b)} (\delta_{a'b'} - p) X_{a'b'} \<\PT \eabp, \eab\>$. Then $\P(\|\mathcal{Q}(\mtx{X})\|_\infty > \lambda \sqrt{\mu_0 r/(np)} \|\mtx{X}\|_\infty) \le 2 n^2 \exp(-\lambda^2/(2 + (2/3)\sqrt{\mu_0 r/(np)} \lambda))$.
conclusions: $\P(\|\mathcal{Q}(\mtx{X})\|_\infty > \lambda \sqrt{\mu_0 r/(np)} \|\mtx{X}\|_\infty) \le 2 n^2 \exp(-\lambda^2/(2 + (2/3)\sqrt{\mu_0 r/(np)} \lambda))$
For $\lambda = \sqrt{6 \beta \log n}$ with $\beta > 2$, the bound is $\le 2 n^{-\beta}$ provided $np \ge (8\beta/3) \mu_0 r \log n$

nodes.name: Diagonal-Sandwich Spectral Bound
nodes.statement: For $\mtx{Z} = \sum_{ab} X_{ab} \<\PT(\eab), \eab\> \eab$: $\|\mtx{Z}\| \le (2 \mu_0 r/n) \|\mtx{X}\|$.
conclusions: $\|\mtx{Z}\| \le (2 \mu_0 r / n) \|\mtx{X}\|$ where $\mtx{Z} = \sum_{ab} X_{ab} \<\PT(\eab), \eab\> \eab$

nodes.name: Off-Diagonal Bound (Lemma teo:PO2)
nodes.statement: $p^{-2} \|\sum_{(a,b) \ne (a',b')} \xi_{ab} \xi_{a'b'} X_{ab} \<\PT(\eabp), \eab\> \eab\| \le C'_0 \sqrt{\mu_0 r} \beta \log n / p \cdot \|\mtx{X}\|_\infty$ w.p. $\ge 1 - O(n^{-\beta})$ when $np \ge 3 \mu_0 r \beta \log n$.
conclusions: $p^{-2} \|\sum_{(a,b) \ne (a',b')} \xi_{ab} \xi_{a'b'} X_{ab} \<\PT(\eabp), \eab\> \eab\| \le C'_0 \sqrt{\mu_0 r} \beta \log n / p \cdot \|\mtx{X}\|_\infty$ with probability $\ge 1 - O(n^{-\beta})$

nodes.name: Hadamard Product Spectral Bound
nodes.statement: For matrices $\mtx{A}, \mtx{B}$: $\|\mtx{A} \circ \mtx{B}\| \le \|\mtx{A}\| \nu(\mtx{B})$, where $\nu(\mtx{B}) = \inf\{c(\mtx{X}) c(\mtx{Y}) : \mtx{X} \mtx{Y}^* = \mtx{B}\}$ and $c(\mtx{X})^2 = \max_i \sum_j X_{ij}^2$.
assumptions: $\mtx{A}, \mtx{B}$ matrices of the same dimension $n_1 \times n_2$
conclusions: $\|\mtx{A} \circ \mtx{B}\| \le \|\mtx{A}\| \nu(\mtx{B})$

nodes.name: $\nu$ Bound on $\mathcal{H}^3(\mtx{E})$
nodes.statement: There exist constants $C, c$ such that $\nu(\mathcal{H}^3(\mtx{E})) \le C \mu_0 r/n$ w.p. $\ge 1 - O(n^{-\beta})$ when $m \ge c \mu_0^{4/3} n r^{5/3} \beta \log n$.
conclusions: $\nu(\mathcal{H}^3(\mtx{E})) \le C \mu_0 r / n$ with probability at least $1 - O(n^{-\beta})$

nodes.name: Maximum Row-Sum Bound for $\vct{\alpha}_j$
nodes.statement: $c([\vct{\alpha}_1, \ldots, \vct{\alpha}_r]) \le C \sqrt{\mu_0 r / n}$ w.p. $\ge 1 - O(n^{-\beta})$ under conditions of LP103.17.
assumptions: $m$ obeys the condition of Lemma teo:HE (LP103.17), $m \ge c \mu_0^{4/3} n r^{5/3} \beta \log n$
conclusions: $c([\vct{\alpha}_1, \ldots, \vct{\alpha}_r]) \le C \sqrt{\mu_0 r / n}$ with probability at least $1 - O(n^{-\beta})$

nodes.name: Bernstein Concentration on $\sum \delta_{ab} E_{ab}^2$
nodes.statement: For integer $1 \le q \le np$ with $np \ge 2 \log n$: $\E_\delta (\max_a \sum_b \delta_{ab} E_{ab}^2)^q \le 2 (2 np \|\mtx{E}\|_\infty^2)^q$.
conclusions: $\E_\delta (\max_a \sum_b \delta_{ab} E_{ab}^2)^q \le 2 (2 np \|\mtx{E}\|_\infty^2)^q$

nodes.name: Talagrand Concentration
nodes.statement: For independent $\{Y_i\}$ and $Y_\star = \sup_{f \in \mathcal{F}} \sum_i f(Y_i)$ with $|f| \le B, \E f(Y_i) = 0$: $\P(|Y_\star - \E Y_\star| > t) \le 3 \exp(-t/(KB) \log(1 + Bt/(\sigma^2 + B \E Y_\star)))$.
assumptions: $\{Y_i\}_{1 \le i \le n}$ independent Banach-valued random variables
conclusions: $\P(|Y_\star - \E Y_\star| > t) \le 3 \exp(-(t/(KB)) \log(1 + Bt/(\sigma^2 + B \E Y_\star)))$ where $\sigma^2 = \sup_f \sum_i \E f^2(Y_i)$

nodes.name: Bound on $H_\omega$ in Order-2 Term
nodes.statement: $\|\mtx{H}\|_\infty \le \frac{\mu_0 r}{np}(3\|\mtx{E}\|_\infty + 2 \mu_0 r/n)$ for the deterministic auxiliary matrix in the order-2 analysis.
assumptions: $\mtx{H}$ defined by $H_{\omega_1} = p^{-1} \sum_{\omega_2 \ne \omega_1} E_{\omega_2} P_{\omega_2 \omega_2} P_{\omega_2 \omega_1}$
conclusions: $\|\mtx{H}\|_\infty \le \frac{\mu_0 r}{np}(3 \|\mtx{E}\|_\infty + 2 \mu_0 r / n)$

nodes.name: Nuclear Norm Minimization (SDP)
nodes.statement: Solve the semidefinite program $\min \|\mtx{X}\|_*$ s.t. $\PO(\mtx{X}) = \PO(\mtx{M})$ via SDPT3 or equivalent.
output: Recovered matrix $\mtx{X}^\star$ with minimum nuclear norm matching observations on $\Omega$
nodes.pseudocode: Equivalent SDP formulation: minimize $\trace(\mtx{W}_1) + \trace(\mtx{W}_2)$ subject to $X_{ij} = M_{ij}$ for $(i,j) \in \Omega$ and $\begin{bmatrix} \mtx{W}_1 & \mtx{X} \\ \mtx{X}^* & \mtx{W}_2 \end{bmatrix} \succeq 0$.

nodes.name: PSD Trace Minimization (Symmetric Variant)
nodes.statement: Solve $\min \trace(\mtx{X})$ s.t. $X_{ij} = M_{ij}$ on $\Omega$ and $\mtx{X} \succeq 0$, the SDP variant when $\mtx{M}$ is positive semidefinite.
input: Observed entries on $\Omega$ of a PSD matrix $\mtx{M}$

nodes.name: Sample-Size Threshold (Main bound)
nodes.statement: $m \ge C \max(\mu_1^2, \mu_0^{1/2} \mu_1, \mu_0 n^{1/4}) \, n r (\beta \log n)$ for the general recovery theorem.

nodes.name: Power-Series Inversion
nodes.statement: $(\PT \PO \PT)^{-1}(\mtx{X}) = p^{-1}(\mtx{X} + \mathcal{H}(\mtx{X}) + \mathcal{H}^2(\mtx{X}) + \ldots)$ where $\mathcal{H} = \PT - p^{-1} \PT \PO \PT$.

nodes.name: Dual Certificate Ansatz
nodes.statement: $\mtx{Y} = \cAOT (\cAOT^* \cAOT)^{-1}(\mtx{E})$ with $\mtx{E} = \sum_{k=1}^r \vct{u}_k \vct{v}_k^*$, the minimum-Frobenius-norm dual matrix.

nodes.name: Phase-Transition Experiments on Full Matrices
nodes.statement: For $n=40, 50$, generate rank-$r$ matrices $\mtx{M} = \mtx{M}_L \mtx{M}_R^*$ with i.i.d. Gaussian factors; declare success if $\|\mtx{X}_{\mathrm{opt}} - \mtx{M}\|_F/\|\mtx{M}\|_F < 10^{-3}$. Plot recovery rate over 50 trials per $(n,m,r)$.

nodes.name: Phase-Transition Experiments on PSD Matrices
nodes.statement: Recovery experiments with $\mtx{M} = \mtx{M}_F \mtx{M}_F^*$ PSD; nuclear-norm SDP with constraint $\mtx{X} \succeq 0$ shows substantially larger recovery region than full-matrix case.

nodes.name: Recovery from Gaussian Projections
nodes.statement: Comparison experiments where $\mtx{M}$ is observed via random Gaussian linear functionals $\mathcal{A}(\mtx{M})$, with recovery via nuclear-norm minimization subject to $\mathcal{A}(\mtx{X}) = \mathcal{A}(\mtx{M})$.

nodes.name: Rank-1 Matrix $\vct{e}_1 \vct{e}_n^*$ (impossibility)
nodes.statement: Counterexample $\mtx{M} = \vct{e}_1 \vct{e}_n^*$ (1 in top-right corner, zero elsewhere) cannot be recovered from a sample of entries unless essentially all are observed; motivates incoherence.

nodes.name: Multitask / Multiclass Learning
nodes.statement: Application: linear classifiers $\vct{w}_k$ for $K$ classes assembled into low-rank $\mtx{W} = [\vct{w}_1, \ldots, \vct{w}_K]$, recoverable from partial label observations via the generalized formulation.

nodes.name: Coupon Collector Lower Bound
nodes.statement: Recovering a rank-1 matrix requires at least one observation per row and column; the coupon collector's problem implies on the order of $n \log n$ samples are necessary, showing that the logarithmic factor in TP103.3 is tight.

nodes.name: Connectivity / Bipartite Graph Necessity
nodes.statement: If the bipartite observation graph (rows-to-columns) is disconnected, then $\PO$ restricted to $T$ has nontrivial null space and rank-1 recovery is impossible; this links injectivity of $\PT \PO \PT$ to graph connectivity.

nodes.name: Bernoulli vs. Uniform Reduction
nodes.statement: Failure probability under uniform sampling of size $m$ is at most twice the failure probability under Bernoulli sampling with $p = m/(n_1 n_2)$, allowing analysis under the simpler independent Bernoulli model.

nodes.name: Optimal Sample Complexity $nr \log n$
nodes.statement: Is exact matrix completion possible with sample size on the order of $nr$ (up to log factors), matching the $(2n-r)r$ degrees of freedom? The current $n^{6/5} r \log n$ exponent is conjectured to be improvable to $nr \log n$.

nodes.name: Approximate Recovery for Approximately Low-Rank Matrices
nodes.statement: Is $\|\mtx{M}_\star - \mtx{M}\|_*$ comparable in order to $\|\mtx{M} - \mtx{M}_r\|_*$ when $\mtx{M}$ is only approximately low-rank? Open whether nuclear-norm SDP achieves the oracle truncation error.

nodes.name: Noise-Robust Matrix Completion
nodes.statement: Under noisy observations $Y_{ij} = M_{ij} + z_{ij}$, can the constrained nuclear-norm SDP $\min \|\mtx{X}\|_*$ s.t. $\|\PO(\mtx{X} - \mtx{Y})\|_F \le \epsilon$ produce a recovery error proportional to the noise level?

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma teo:unicity (Uniqueness via Dual Certificate)
nodes.statement: Use convex perturbation: any feasible perturbation $\mtx{H}$ obeys $\mathcal{R}_\Omega(\mtx{H}) = 0$; combine subgradient inequality with the spectral bound on $\PTc(\mtx{Y})$ and the injectivity assumption to show $\|\mtx{X}_0 + \mtx{H}\|_* > \|\mtx{X}_0\|_*$ unless $\mtx{H} = 0$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem teo:rudelson
nodes.statement: Decompose $\PT \PO \PT = \sum_{ab} \delta_{ab} \PT(\eab) \otimes \PT(\eab)$ and apply Rudelson's selection theorem (TP103.5) plus Talagrand concentration to obtain the deviation bound.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem teo:main2 (Main Recovery Theorem)
nodes.statement: Combine the four/five spectral bounds (Lemmas teo:order0--teo:order3 and teo:highorder) with $k_0 \in \{3,4\}$ to bound $\|\PTc(\mtx{Y})\| < 1$, then invoke LP103.4 to conclude uniqueness.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma teo:gaussian (Random Orthogonal Coherence)
nodes.statement: Use chi-squared concentration (LP103.3) for $\|\mtx{P}_U \vct{e}_i\|^2$, then apply Hoeffding for the second claim about $\|\sum_k \vct{u}_k \vct{v}_k^*\|_\infty$ via a Rademacher-symmetrization argument.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma teo:order0
nodes.statement: Symmetrize via independent copy and Rademacher signs, apply noncommutative Khintchine (LP103.11), reduce to bounding $\max_a \sum_b \delta_{ab} E_{ab}^2$ via LP103.19, then conclude via Markov.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma teo:order1
nodes.statement: Decompose $\mtx{S}$ into diagonal $\mtx{S}_0$ and off-diagonal $\mtx{S}_1$ contributions; bound each via Theorem teo:PO, decoupling (LP103.12), and Bernstein-type estimate LP103.13.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma teo:order2
nodes.statement: Partition $p^{-1}(\PO - p\OpId)\mathcal{H}^2(\mtx{E})$ into five terms based on coincidences among $\omega_1, \omega_2, \omega_3$; bound each via decoupling, Lemma teo:lemma0p (LP103.14), Lemma teo:PO2 (LP103.15), and Theorem teo:PO.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma teo:order3 (and teo:HE)
nodes.statement: Express $p^{-1}(\PO - p\OpId)\mathcal{H}^3(\mtx{E}) = p^{-1}(\Xi \circ \mathcal{H}^3(\mtx{E}))$, apply Hadamard product bound (LP103.16) with $\nu(\mathcal{H}^3(\mtx{E})) \le C \mu_0 r/n$ from Lemma teo:HE (LP103.17), and combine with $\|\Xi\|$ bound from Theorem teo:PO.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma teo:highorder
nodes.statement: Bound spectral by Frobenius norm, use Corollary teo:POPT (CP103.1) and the geometric series $\|\sum_{k \ge k_0} \mathcal{H}^k(\mtx{E})\|_F \le \|\mathcal{H}\|^{k_0}/(1 - \|\mathcal{H}\|) \sqrt{r}$, with $\|\mathcal{H}\|$ controlled by Theorem teo:rudelson.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma teo:incoherentbases
nodes.statement: Apply Hoeffding's inequality to $Z_{ij} = \sum_k \epsilon_k u_{ik} v_{jk}$, taking the union bound over $n^2$ entries.

nodes.name: Setup: subgradient form for nuclear norm
nodes.statement: Use $\sum_k \vct{u}_k \vct{v}_k^* + \mtx{W}^0$ as a subgradient at $\mtx{X}_0$ for any $\mtx{W}^0 \in T^\perp$ with $\|\mtx{W}^0\| \le 1$; obtain $\|\mtx{X}_0 + \mtx{H}\|_* \ge \|\mtx{X}_0\|_* + \<\sum_k \vct{u}_k \vct{v}_k^* + \mtx{W}^0, \mtx{H}\>$.

nodes.name: Substitute the dual certificate
nodes.statement: Let $\mtx{W} = \PTc(\mtx{Y})$ and write $\sum_k \vct{u}_k \vct{v}_k^* = \mathcal{R}_\Omega^* \lambda - \mtx{W}$; using $\|\mtx{W}\| < 1$ and $\mathcal{R}_\Omega(\mtx{H}) = 0$, deduce $\|\mtx{X}_0 + \mtx{H}\|_* \ge \|\mtx{X}_0\|_* + \<\mtx{W}^0 - \mtx{W}, \mtx{H}\>$.

nodes.name: Choose dualizing $\mtx{W}^0$ and apply duality
nodes.statement: Pick $\mtx{W}^0 = \PTc(\mtx{Z})$ with $\<\mtx{Z}, \PTc(\mtx{H})\> = \|\PTc(\mtx{H})\|_*$ (Lemma teo:dual). Then $\<\mtx{W}^0 - \mtx{W}, \mtx{H}\> \ge (1 - \|\mtx{W}\|) \|\PTc(\mtx{H})\|_*$, strictly positive unless $\PTc(\mtx{H}) = 0$.

nodes.name: Conclude via injectivity
nodes.statement: If $\PTc(\mtx{H}) = 0$ then $\mtx{H} \in T$; combined with $\mathcal{R}_\Omega(\mtx{H}) = 0$ and the injectivity assumption, $\mtx{H} = 0$, proving uniqueness.

nodes.name: Operator decomposition $\PT \PO \PT = \sum_{ab} \delta_{ab} \PT(\eab) \otimes \PT(\eab)$
nodes.statement: Write $\PT(\mtx{X}) = \sum_{ab} \<\mtx{X}, \PT(\eab)\> \eab$ and derive the rank-one operator sum representation.

nodes.name: Bound $\|\PT(\eab)\|_F^2 \le 2 \mu_0 r / \min(n_1, n_2)$
nodes.statement: From the explicit formula for $\PT(\eab)$, derive $\|\PT(\eab)\|_F^2 = \|\mtx{P}_U \vct{e}_a\|^2 + \|\mtx{P}_V \vct{e}_b\|^2 - \|\mtx{P}_U \vct{e}_a\|^2 \|\mtx{P}_V \vct{e}_b\|^2$ and bound by $2\mu_0 r/\min(n_1,n_2)$.

nodes.name: Apply Rudelson selection (TP103.5) for $\E Z$
nodes.statement: Use Rudelson's selection theorem to bound $\E Z \le C'_R \sqrt{\mu_0 nr \log n / m}$.

nodes.name: Apply Talagrand concentration
nodes.statement: Bound $|Z - \E Z|$ via the Talagrand-style inequality (LP103.20) to obtain the final probability bound $1 - 3 n^{-\beta}$.

nodes.name: Bound $\|\PTc(\mathcal{R}_\Omega^* \lambda)\|$ via series expansion
nodes.statement: Use the Neumann-series expansion $\PTc(\mtx{Y}) = p^{-1} (\PTc \PO \PT)(\mtx{E} + \mathcal{H}(\mtx{E}) + \mathcal{H}^2(\mtx{E}) + \ldots)$ to decompose into successive order terms.

nodes.name: Combine order-0,1,2 lemmas with high-order tail at $k_0=3$
nodes.statement: Apply Lemmas teo:order0 (LP103.6), teo:order1 (LP103.7), teo:order2 (LP103.8), and teo:highorder (LP103.10) with $k_0 = 3$ to obtain $\|\PTc(\mtx{Y})\| < 1$ under $m \ge C \max(\mu_1^2, \mu_0^{1/2} \mu_1, \mu_0^{4/3} r^{1/3}, \mu_0 n^{1/4}) nr \beta \log n$.

nodes.name: Small-rank refinement using order-3 lemma at $k_0=4$
nodes.statement: For $r \le \mu_0^{-1} n^{1/5}$, additionally invoke teo:order3 (LP103.9) with $k_0 = 4$ and use $\mu_1 \le \mu_0 \sqrt{r}$ to reduce the bound to $m \ge C \mu_0 n^{6/5} r \beta \log n$.

nodes.name: Conclude via uniqueness lemma LP103.4
nodes.statement: Together with Theorem teo:rudelson establishing injectivity of $\PT \PO \PT$, invoke LP103.4 to conclude unique recovery.

nodes.name: Reduce to chi-squared and use $Z_r = Y_r/Y_n$
nodes.statement: Recognize $\|\mtx{P}_U \vct{e}_i\|^2$ as the squared length of the first $r$ components of a random unit vector, distributed as $Y_r/Y_n$ with $Y_d \sim \chi^2_d$.

nodes.name: Apply chi-squared concentration
nodes.statement: Use LP103.3 to bound $\P(Z_r - r/n \ge 16 \sqrt{r \log n}/n) \le 2 n^{-3}$, then take union over $i$.

nodes.name: Hoeffding for the size-of-sign matrix
nodes.statement: By Rademacher symmetrization, $\mtx{F} = \sum_k \epsilon_k \vct{u}_k \vct{v}_k^*$ has the same distribution as $\mtx{E}$; conditional Hoeffding plus the bound on $\|\mtx{P}_U \vct{e}_i\|^2$ yields $\|\mtx{F}\|_\infty \le C (\log n) \sqrt{\bar r}/n$.

nodes.name: Symmetrize $\mtx{S}$ via independent copy and Rademacher signs
nodes.statement: Use Jensen + symmetrization to reduce to bounding $(\E \|\mtx{S}_\epsilon\|^q)^{1/q}$ where $\mtx{S}_\epsilon$ is the Rademacher-randomized version.

nodes.name: Apply noncommutative Khintchine
nodes.statement: Invoke LP103.11 with $q' \ge \log n$ to bound the $S_{q'}$-norm by a max of two diagonal-matrix norms.

nodes.name: Bound $\E (\max_a \sum_b \delta_{ab} E_{ab}^2)^q$
nodes.statement: Invoke LP103.19 to bound the diagonal matrix norm by $4 (2 np \|\mtx{E}\|_\infty^2)^q$.

nodes.name: Markov tail and choice of $q$
nodes.statement: With $q = \beta \log n$, $t = e$, conclude $\P(\|\mtx{S}\| > Ce \mu_1 \sqrt{nr \beta \log n /m}) \le n^{-\beta}$.

nodes.name: Decompose $\mtx{S} = \mtx{S}_0 + \mtx{S}_1$
nodes.statement: Split into diagonal ($(a,b) = (a',b')$) and off-diagonal contributions.

nodes.name: Bound $\|\mtx{S}_0\|$ via Theorem teo:PO and Lemma teo:lemma0p
nodes.statement: Use $\xi_{ab}^2 = (1-2p)\xi_{ab} + p(1-p)$, then apply TP103.4 and LP103.14 on the deterministic part.

nodes.name: Decouple and apply Bernstein on $\mtx{S}_1$
nodes.statement: Use LP103.12 to decouple, then control $\|\mtx{H}\|_\infty$ via LP103.13 (Bernstein for $\mathcal{Q}(\mtx{X})$) and combine with TP103.4.

nodes.name: Partition into 5 cases by coincidence of $\omega_i$
nodes.statement: Partition $p^{-1}(\PO-p\OpId)\mathcal{H}^2(\mtx{E}) = $ (all equal) $+$ (two pairs of cases) $+$ (all distinct), five terms in total.

nodes.name: Bound diagonal term ($\omega_1 = \omega_2 = \omega_3$)
nodes.statement: Use TP103.4 and LP103.14 to bound by $C (nr/m)^2 (\mu_0^2 \mu_1 \sqrt{nr \beta \log n / m} + \mu_0^2)$.

nodes.name: Bound mixed terms via decoupling and Lemma teo:PO2
nodes.statement: Apply LP103.12 to the three two-equal cases; use LP103.15 (teo:PO2) and LP103.13 (teo:bernstein) to control the resulting random matrix norms.

nodes.name: Triple-decoupling for the all-distinct term
nodes.statement: Use a triple-variable decoupling inequality to reduce to independent Rademacher chaos, then apply Bernstein twice to bound by $C \mu_0 \mu_1 (nr \beta \log n / m)^{3/2}$.

nodes.name: Combine to bound $p^{-1}\|(\PO-p\OpId)\mathcal{H}^2(\mtx{E})\|$
nodes.statement: Sum the five contributions and verify that $m \ge \lambda \mu_0^{4/3} n r^{4/3} \beta \log n$ implies the bound $C \lambda^{-3/2}$.

nodes.name: Hadamard-product reformulation
nodes.statement: Recognize $p^{-1}(\PO - p\OpId) \mathcal{H}^3(\mtx{E}) = p^{-1}(\Xi \circ \mathcal{H}^3(\mtx{E}))$ where $\Xi$ has i.i.d. entries $\xi_{ab}$.

nodes.name: Bound $\|\Xi\|$ via Theorem teo:PO
nodes.statement: Apply TP103.4 with $\mtx{Z} = \mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^*$ to obtain $p^{-1} \|\Xi\| \le C \sqrt{n^3 \beta \log n / m}$.

nodes.name: Bound $\nu(\mathcal{H}^3(\mtx{E}))$ via Lemma teo:HE
nodes.statement: Use the explicit factorization $\mathcal{H}^3(\mtx{E}) = \mtx{X} \mtx{Y}^*$ from the SVD-induced decomposition; bound row norms by LP103.18 to obtain $\nu \le C \mu_0 r/n$.

nodes.name: Combine via Ando-Horn-Johnson
nodes.statement: Apply LP103.16 to combine the two bounds, yielding $p^{-1} \|\Xi \circ \mathcal{H}^3(\mtx{E})\| \le C \sqrt{\mu_0^2 nr^2 \beta \log n / m}$, hence $\le C_3 \lambda^{-1/2}$.

nodes.name: Reduce spectral to Frobenius norm
nodes.statement: Use $\|(\PTc \PO \PT)(\cdot)\| \le \|(\PO \PT)(\cdot)\|_F$ and apply Corollary CP103.1 to get $p^{-1} \|(\PO \PT) \sum_k \mathcal{H}^k(\mtx{E})\|_F \le \sqrt{3/2p} \|\sum_k \mathcal{H}^k(\mtx{E})\|_F$.

nodes.name: Geometric series tail bound
nodes.statement: $\|\sum_{k \ge k_0} \mathcal{H}^k(\mtx{E})\|_F \le \|\mathcal{H}\|^{k_0}/(1 - \|\mathcal{H}\|) \|\mtx{E}\|_F$, with $\|\mathcal{H}\|$ bounded by Theorem teo:rudelson and $\|\mtx{E}\|_F = \sqrt{r}$.

nodes.name: Reformulate as semidefinite program
nodes.statement: Transform $\min \|\mtx{X}\|_*$ s.t. $\PO(\mtx{X}) = \PO(\mtx{M})$ into the SDP $\min \trace(\mtx{W}_1) + \trace(\mtx{W}_2)$ s.t. $X_{ij} = M_{ij}$ on $\Omega$ and $\begin{bmatrix} \mtx{W}_1 & \mtx{X} \\ \mtx{X}^* & \mtx{W}_2 \end{bmatrix} \succeq 0$.

nodes.name: Solve via interior-point SDP solver
nodes.statement: Pass the SDP to an off-the-shelf solver such as SDPT3 to obtain the optimum $(\mtx{X}^\star, \mtx{W}_1^\star, \mtx{W}_2^\star)$.

nodes.name: Return $\mtx{X}^\star$
nodes.statement: Output $\mtx{X}^\star$ as the recovered matrix; under the conditions of TP103.2, $\mtx{X}^\star = \mtx{M}$ with high probability.
